strings.name: Beatrice Fihn
strings.role: Founder and director of Lex International; former ICAN executive director
strings.summary: Fihn is a Swedish legal professional and disarmament advocate who led the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN), mobilising civil society in the nuclear-ban treaty process. She now leads Lex International and is a senior fellow at the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research, working on international law, research funding and public communication.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026. Recent records include production credits published on 16 November and 2026 programme release information; these do not establish same-day recording or physical attendance. Only the birth year, 1982, is confirmed.
strings.influence.rationale: Led the International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons and helped advance the nuclear weapons prohibition treaty; the organisation received the Nobel Peace Prize.
strings.facts.f1.label: Higher education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor's degree in international relations from Stockholm University and master's degree in law from University College London. Exact graduation years were not independently confirmed in this review.
strings.facts.f2.label: Nobel Prize recipient
strings.facts.f2.value: The 2017 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to ICAN. Fihn and Hiroshima survivor Setsuko Thurlow accepted it and delivered the lecture on the organisation's behalf; they were not each awarded an individual prize.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Mobilising civil society for the nuclear-ban treaty
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led ICAN's international advocacy for prohibiting nuclear weapons; states negotiated and adopted the treaty. Its entry into force was a legal milestone, not the elimination of nuclear weapons worldwide.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Supporting international law through philanthropy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Lex International is a philanthropic fund hosted by Swiss Philanthropy Foundation, supporting research, communication and cooperation across institutions. Its projects are not all attributed to her as an individual creator.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Trenchers work page published production credits
strings.timeline.t1.text: Little Black Book's Pin Drop work page lists her among the executive producers. Trevor McMahan directed; McMahan and Blaine Kneece wrote the work. The date is the page's publication date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Hosted a biosecurity conversation
strings.timeline.t2.text: Lex's Summit Talks page lists her conversation with Filippa Lentzos for release in May, addressing biosecurity and international rules. The release month does not establish the recording date.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Founded and began leading Lex International
strings.timeline.t3.text: The organisation's biography identifies her as founder and director since 2023. Swiss Philanthropy Foundation hosts the fund.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Stepped down as ICAN executive director
strings.timeline.t4.text: Ended her executive-director service. ICAN announced the planned departure in November 2022, then announced in August 2023 that Melissa Parke would start on 1 September; there was no same-day direct handover.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Nuclear weapons prohibition treaty entered into force
strings.timeline.t5.text: The treaty entered into force after meeting its ratification requirements. This was distinct from adoption and opening for signature in 2017; signing does not automatically make a state a party.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Accepted ICAN's prize with Setsuko Thurlow
strings.timeline.t6.text: At the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony in Oslo, the two delivered the Nobel Lecture for the winning organisation, emphasising the humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapons.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Nuclear-ban treaty adopted
strings.timeline.t7.text: A UN negotiating conference adopted the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, with ICAN helping mobilise civil-society support. It opened for signature on 20 September that year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Began leading ICAN
strings.timeline.t8.text: Became executive director, coordinating international civil-society advocacy. Previously worked on disarmament at the Women's International League for Peace and Freedom and its Reaching Critical Will project.
